title: India's Fiscal Deficit Hits Rs 7.14 Lakh Crore, 42.1% of Full-Year Target in First Half
excerpt: The Centre's April-September deficit widened from Rs 5.7 lakh crore a year earlier as subsidy spending hit Rs 2.2 lakh crore on costlier petroleum and fertilisers, while capital expenditure rose to Rs 6.5 lakh crore, CGA data showed on Friday.
body:
• India's fiscal deficit for April-September stood at Rs 7.14 lakh crore ($75.24 billion), 42.1 percent of the full-year target of Rs 16.96 lakh crore, government data showed on Friday.
  • The deficit widened from Rs 5.7 lakh crore in the same period last year, driven by a subsidy bill of Rs 2.2 lakh crore — 54 percent of the full-year subsidy target spent in six months.
  • Capital expenditure rose to Rs 6.5 lakh crore from Rs 5.8 lakh crore a year earlier, while net tax receipts grew to Rs 12.76 lakh crore.
  • The full-year target is 4.3 percent of GDP, down from the 4.4 percent achieved in 2025-26 — the consolidation path the government says it remains on.

India's fiscal deficit in the first half of the financial year stood at Rs 7.14 lakh crore, or 42.1 percent of the target for the year ending March, government data showed on Friday, according to Reuters. The deficit in the same period last year stood at Rs 5.7 lakh crore.

The Centre has budgeted a fiscal deficit of Rs 16.96 lakh crore for 2026-27, equal to 4.3 percent of GDP. At the half-year mark, the government has therefore used a little over two-fifths of its full-year borrowing room, broadly in line with the seasonal pattern in which revenue collections are back-loaded.

Subsidies Did the Damage

The widening came from the expenditure side. The Centre's subsidy outgo in the first six months rose to Rs 2.2 lakh crore, IANS reported, as the continuing Middle East conflict pushed up prices of petroleum products and fertilisers. The outgo was 54 percent of the full-year target of Rs 4.1 lakh crore, compared with 53 percent in the first half of last year.

Within that total, food subsidy expenditure stood at Rs 1.02 lakh crore, urea subsidy at Rs 85,585 crore, nutrient-based fertiliser subsidies at Rs 33,664 crore and petroleum subsidies at Rs 1,149 crore.

Total government expenditure in the six months was Rs 25.5 lakh crore, against Rs 23 lakh crore a year earlier. Capital expenditure on highway, rail and port projects rose to Rs 6.5 lakh crore from Rs 5.8 lakh crore in the first half of the previous year — the growth-and-jobs component of spending the government has prioritised even as the deficit widened.

Receipts Held Up

On the revenue side, total receipts stood at Rs 18.35 lakh crore in April-September, 50.3 percent of the full-year budget estimate, up from 49.5 percent at the same point last year. Revenue receipts were Rs 17.57 lakh crore, 49.7 percent of the estimate, comprising net tax revenue of Rs 12.76 lakh crore and non-tax revenue of Rs 4.81 lakh crore.

Net tax revenue reached 44.5 percent of the full-year estimate, compared with 43.3 percent in the same period last year — receipts are running slightly ahead of last year's pace even as spending accelerated.

The Consolidation Question

The government achieved its fiscal deficit target of 4.4 percent of GDP in 2025-26 and has lowered the target to 4.3 percent for the current year as part of its consolidation path. A first-half print of 42.1 percent of the annual target does not threaten that goal by itself; the risk sits in the subsidy line, where more than half the year's allocation is already spent and the driver — imported energy and fertiliser prices — is outside the government's control.

For bond and currency markets, the figure to watch in the second half is whether subsidy spending slows as the winter crop cycle ends, and whether the capex pace holds. If both happen, the 4.3 percent target remains reachable without a late-year spending squeeze.
